name: Link-cable exchange buffer (RX and TX)
notes: The serial interrupt handler 00:2AE9 stores each received byte at [$DC48:$DC49] + index and loads the next byte to send from [$DC4A:$DC4B] + index + 1 (index = $DC4C:$DC4D, 00:2C88-2CB2; a high index byte of $FF skips the store). 00:2D5F sets $DC47=$10 (00:2D5F-2D61) and both base pointers to $C000 ($DC48:$DC49 at 00:2DB2-2DB9, $DC4A:$DC4B at 00:2DBC-2DC4); 00:2E0E and 00:2E41 re-point $DC4A:$DC4B to $C000 again and set the command byte $DC56 (or $40 / or $80). The transfer ends when the index high byte equals [$DC47] (00:2CB5-2CBD): $10 = $1000 bytes, i.e. exactly one slot-sized buffer exchanged in place; the handler sets $DC47=$08 ($0800 bytes) when the header byte has bit 7 set (00:2C4B, 00:2C73). What the $0800 variant carries: ?. Bank 7 prepares the buffer in Bank007_State04 / State13 (07:43E9-4411, 07:475D-4785): clear $1000 bytes, load the slot (02:4C80) and the owner (02:5054) and put [$DA56] at $CFFF; after the exchange Bank007_State09/17 (07:45FD-4616, 07:48A1-48BA) read $CFFF (07:4A17-4A24) and call 02:462F to store the buffer as a received photo. The link state variables $DC43-$DC5E are described in `wram_dc00`.

name: [8] print page read back from VRAM
type: 240 tiles x 16 B (16 x 15 tiles): $C000-$C7FF = VRAM $9000-$97FF, $C800-$CEFF = VRAM $8800-$8EFF
notes: After drawing the print layout with far calls to bank 9 (09:461E, 463F, 465F, 4687, 46C6, 4706, 474D, 4775, 45B0 = thumbnail upload) Bank008 (08:46A3-4770) reads the composed tiles back into WRAM and sets the 3-byte source pointer [$DB4D]=$00, [$DB4E]=$C0, [$DB4F]=$00 (= $C000, bank 0, 08:4750-475A) and [$DB6D]=4, [$D5CE]=$1D (08:475D-4776). The other two branches (08:4617-461F, 08:4663-466B) point $DB4D-$DB4F at the photo returned by 02:517B instead. The consumer of $DB4D (printer packet builder in bank 0) was not traced here: ?.

name: Photo image (slot bytes 000-DFF)
type: 224 tiles x 16 B, 2bpp tile format; 16 tiles per row, 14 rows (tile row = $100 B)
notes: The 128x112-pixel picture being viewed / shot / edited / printed (or the Game Face). "Album layout" used by banks 2, 4, 6, 7, 8: $C000-$C7FF <-> VRAM $9000 (128 tiles), $C800-$C8FF <-> $8800 (16 tiles), $C900-$CDFF <-> $8000 (80 tiles) (02:5121-5148, 04:57F1-5816, 06:511D-513F, 07:4411-4436, 07:6A1E-6A3D); bank 3 layout is $C000-$C7FF <-> $9000 and $C800-$CDFF <-> $8800 ($600 bytes, 03:6625-663E). Effect-table entry offsets (06:73EF-7477, 0A:5A01-5A70): row 4 = $C400, row 7 = $C700 (left half $C700, right half $C780), row 10 = $CA00, tile (3,3) = $C330. 02:4005-402D sums and 02:4031-405A XORs exactly $E016 = $E00 bytes of it into $DA8F/$DA90 (the checksum stored at tag F34-F35). Whole-slot sources: 02:4C80 (A = photo number) copies $FB8 bytes from SRAM (slot found with 02:444D, bank = slot/2+1, $A000 or $B000, 02:4C8A-4CB1) when A < $1E and A < [$D561]; for A < $1E but A >= [$D561] it copies the ROM placeholder bank $36 $5000 (02:4CB6-4CC1); for A >= $1E it copies a ROM image: bank $36 $4000 for the locked case (02:4D05, A-$1E in $10..$17, 02:4CC7-4CE1), otherwise from the 3-byte (lo,hi,bank) table at 02:5218 indexed by A-$1E (02:4CE7-4CFF). The 3584-byte Game Face uses the same bytes: 02:4C37 writes $E00 bytes to SRAM $B1FC, 02:506A reads them back plain, 02:508C-50B8 re-assembles them from four 7-row x $80-byte pieces at SRAM $B1FC/$B27C/$B8FC/$B97C (row stride $100).

name: [3] photo effect/transition sequences on the VRAM copy
notes: 03:66DC: reads VRAM $9000/$8800 back into $C000/$C800 ($0586, 03:66E1-66F5), then 4 passes of a bit-plane operation [hl+1] |= [hl] / [hl] = ~[hl+1]^[hl] over $700 byte pairs (03:66FB-670F) with a re-upload after each pass (03:6713-672A); further variants reload the photo (02:4C80, [$D5FB]) and apply or / $FF-fill (03:6731-6779). 03:67D5/6801/6901/6983 toggle [$FFB0] (palette/flash shadow, see `wram_hram`) and re-upload $C000-$CDFF (03:67E3-67FA). No direct caller was found for these entry points (probably dispatched through a pointer table). 03:6587 (A=VRAM tile, C=photo tile $C000+16C) and 03:65B3 copy one tile between the buffer and VRAM (03:65A2, 65D8); 03:633F-63E3 loads photo [$D5D8] (02:4C80) and uploads in bank-3 layout.

name: [3] reduced preview image (64x56 px)
notes: [$D72B] is a delay counter (03:5C2D-5C3D): when it equals 5, 03:5C40-5C64 reduces photo [$D717] (bit 7 -> +$1E special photos; pointer from 02:517B) with 00:2656 into $C000-$C37F and, when 00:2656 returns NC, uploads it to VRAM $9100 (bc=$0380, 03:5C78-5C83); on carry the joypad shadows $FFA7-$FFA9 are copied to $FFA1-$FFA3 and [$D72B] is cleared (03:5C67-5C77); the counter otherwise runs on to $FF and stops, who re-arms it is ?. Probably a live preview while the cursor moves (I).

name: [6] two-photo blend rows
type: 2 x $100 B: tile row of photo A at $C000, of photo B at $C100; result left in $C000
notes: For each of the 14 tile rows (06:578D, bc=$0E00): 06:57C3 copies row c ($100 B, call $0450) of photo [$D7F7] to $C000 and of [$D7F8] to $C100 (source from 02:517B), 06:57F6-586E mixes them in place with the masks $55/$AA (bit-interleave / dither of two 2bpp rows, 128 iterations, mask rotated each pass), and 06:57A5-57AC uploads $100 B from $C000 to VRAM page table[$57B5+c] = $90..$97, $88, $80..$84 (album layout rows).

name: [5] tile staging for a 4-row level display
type: 4 blocks x $80 B (8 tiles), uploaded to VRAM $9000/$9100/$9200/$9300
notes: 05:6F92 (A = value, C = column 0..31) writes bar patterns at $C001 + ((c&$10)<<4) + ((c&$0C)<<4)... (05:6F95-6FA3): the staging area is $C000-$C1FF; 05:6FFA (called from 05:4789) counts [$D8F2] down: at 3 -> nothing, at 1 $C000/$C080 -> $9000/$9100, at 0 $C100/$C180 -> $9200/$9300 (05:6FFA-7041, call $05F8). The 32-value source is [$D8D1+8k] (see `wram_d800`). Display meaning: I (level bars).

name: [4] icon tile buffer 1 (30 tiles)
notes: Built from the graphics source $C3C0 by 04:5AAD: 16-byte groups copied to $C000 with +$10 gaps (04:5AC7-5AD6); uploaded to $8A00 (bc=$01E0). Used by the album/VIEW cursor icons ([$D63D] selects the entry).

name: [6] 2:1 reduced image rows (output of 00:27F4)
type: 224 x 2 bytes (plane0,plane1) of one pixel row each, consumed in pairs
notes: The output is copied byte pair by byte pair into VRAM with the safe writer $0744, skipping 2 bytes in between (every other pixel row): $9700 x64 pairs and $8800 x160 pairs (06:5631-5647); the second image goes to $9702/$8802 (06:5678-568E) so two images are interleaved line by line. Exact semantic of $27F4 (7x8 blocks, ld c,$07/$08 at 00:2816-281B): ? beyond that.

name: [6] 4x4-tile thumbnail grid (output of 00:2734)
type: 16 tiles x 16 B, row-major (4 tiles per row), 32x28 px: last tile row only 8 bytes per tile valid
notes: Each routine reduces one 64x56-px quadrant (source = photo pointer from 02:517B for [$D7F9..$D7FC], plus offset 0, $600, $80, ... passed on the stack) with 00:2734 into this grid and uploads it in pieces: quadrants 1/3 (06:5414, 5512): $C000 (64 B) -> $9700/$9740, $C040 -> $9780/$97C0, $C080 -> $8800/$8840, then the 8-byte half-tiles $C0C0,$C0D0,$C0E0,$C0F0 -> $8880/$8890/$88A0/$88B0 (resp. $88C0...); quadrants 2/4 (06:5491, 5593) start 4 pixel rows lower, so their first row uses the second 8 bytes of each tile ($C008,$C018,$C028,$C038 -> $8888,$8898,...) and then $C040,$C080,$C0C0 (64 B each) -> $8900,$8980,$8A00. (ld de,$C0C0 at 03:6642/04:504B is a false positive, see header.)

name: [5] packed settings preset (staging)
notes: 05:627A: a3 indexes the 3-byte (lo,hi,bank) pointer table at 05:62A3, $59 bytes are copied to $C000 (call $0450), then 02:4F27 is far-called with DE=$C000 (HL=DE, 02:4F27-4F29) and unpacks them into $D93D... (02:4F2E-4FA6: $D93D,$D93F,$D942,$D945,$D955,$D965,$D985,...,$D9D1,$D9D2). The record layout equals the settings block at SRAM $B061 (02:4F2B-4F2F).

name: [8] animation script (frame, duration) list
type: pairs (frame number, duration), end marker $FF at $C030, $C031 = 0
notes: 08:74F1 copies 12 BG-map entries x 4 rows from VRAM $9814 and $9834 (rows 0,2 into the even bytes of $C000-$C02F, rows 1,3 into the odd bytes, 08:74F4-7513) - i.e. the animation script is stored as tile numbers in the print-screen tilemap (bank $3F $7280, loaded at 08:726B-7274) - then writes $C030=$FF (end marker) and $C031=$00 (08:7516-751C). 08:7483: hl = $C000 + 2[$D500]; byte 0 = frame number (compared with [$D815], new frame -> 08:74B0 uploads $900 B to VRAM $8000 and $500 B to $9000 from a 3-byte table at 08:74DC), byte 1 = duration ([$D510] counts up, 08:7497-749B); $FF as the next entry advances differently (08:749D-74A7). [$D500] is the same animation step counter that 08:4EBB advances modulo 5 (cross-reference for the owner of $D500).

name: [9] anim phase / frame index
notes: Zeroed by the init of states 18-20 (09:4D22, 4D9A, 4E45, 4F06). State19: toggles 0/1 every 8th frame (09:4DF2-4E0C) to pick one of two BG-map halves ($7D00/$7EA0 of bank $1C -> $98A0, 09:4E11-4E1D). State20: index 0..3 (and $03, 09:4EC0) of the jitter pair at $C006+2i. State21: sprite/frame number 0..12 (cp $0D, 09:5000-5004; table at 09:509C, 4 bytes/entry; also the sprite tile a=[$C000]+$B8, 09:503B). State23: slide index 0..3 (cp $04, 09:5108; table 09:5145).

name: [9] frame timer (divider)
notes: Counts frames: State19/20 inc; cp $08; wrap (events every 8th frame); State21 [$C001]+1 < table[$509F+4[C000]] else wrap (09:4FED-4FF5); State23 [$C001]+1 < table[$5148+4[C000]] (09:50EE-50F6).

name: [9] sprite phase
notes: State20 (09:4F9D-4FC8): after 16 frames ([$C003] wraps) advances 0..5 (cp $06) and selects a sprite template word from the table at 09:4FC9 (call $2464, bank-2 template table). State23 (09:5155-517C): 0..4 selects one of 5 BG maps (3-byte pointers at 09:517D, $240 bytes -> $9800).

name: [9] sub-divider / loop counter
notes: State20: inc; and $0F frame divider driving [$C002] (09:4F9D-4FA3). State23: slide loop counter, >= $0A triggers 09:5155 (09:512D-5138).

name: [9] script finished flag
notes: Set to 1 by the scroll engine sub-state 5 (09:40FB-40FD) when the script ends; State21 leaves the loop when it is non-zero (09:5049-504E).

name: [9] step counter / toggle
notes: State19 counts steps to $34 (09:4E1F-4E26), State20 to $43 (09:4EDE-4EE8) then switches screen; State21 toggles 0/1 (xor $01, 09:5007-5009) to choose the tile destination $8000/$8500 (09:500C-5018) and the sprite palette byte from 09:509A.

name: [9] four (dx,dy) jitter pairs
notes: State20 (09:4EC8-4EE5): pair [C000] is refreshed with random(3)-1 twice (call $09D4, 09:4EDB); 09:4F6A-4F84 draws 8 sprites at table positions (09:4F85) with +[$C006+i] added to the Y of each (call $2464-family $2464/$2496). Zeroed at the end of State19 (09:4E54-4E5D).

name: [9] scroll-engine sub-state
notes: Index of the 11-entry rst $18 table at 09:4004 (09:4000-4003): handlers 401A, 4026, 4053, 4084, 40A4, 40C5, 4106, 4137, 4157, 4179, 4105(ret). Zeroed by State20's end (09:4F12); the engine is run once per frame by Bank009_State21 (09:4FDC). It is a tilemap scroll player (sections of 32-byte BG rows kept in $C018+, copied from bank $29 $4000+32n by 00:1720, then scrolled into BG rows $9800+32(row&$1F) with 05F8/0721): meaning of the sub-states 0-10 = I, variables below = C.

name: [9] scroll: ROM source row
notes: Row index (x32) into the bank-$29 source at $4000 (09:4031-403B); advanced by the row count returned in B by 00:1720 (09:4041-4045).

name: [9] scroll: buffer write row
notes: Destination row in the $C018 buffer ($C018+32n, 09:4026-4030); set to the count d at the end of the row-type scan (09:41B6) or 0 (09:414E, 4170).

name: [9] scroll: display row
notes: Row currently shown from the $C018 buffer ($C018+32n, 09:4056-405D), +1/+2 per step, cap $1E/$10 (09:40D3-40DD, 41B2).

name: [9] scroll: BG row cursor
notes: BG-map row counter, pre-decremented (09:4202-4203, 4237-4238); the VRAM row is $9800 + 32(([C012]-1)&$1F) (09:4206-420E); compared with [$C014] (09:422F-4232).

name: [9] scroll: record byte 0 (flag)
notes: From byte 0 of the 5-byte control record at $C018+32[C011]: non-zero -> sub-state 4/8 (loop), zero -> next (09:4073-4083, 4126-4136).

name: [9] scroll: stop row
notes: Record byte 2 (or $FC) = the value of [$C012] at which the scroll step ends (09:4232, 4270).

name: [9] scroll: record byte 3 (pause)
notes: Pause counter in sub-state 5: while joypad $FFA1 is 0 and [$C015] is non-zero it counts [$C011] to $1E then decrements itself (09:40C5-40E0).

name: [9] scroll: record byte 4 (type)
notes: Exit selector: 0 -> keep scrolling, 1 -> next sub-state, 2 -> sub-state 9, else [$C004]=1 and sub-state 10 (09:40E5-4105).

name: [9] scroll: tilemap row buffer
type: rows of 32 bytes (BG-map tile numbers; first 5 bytes of a row also hold the control record)
notes: At least 30 rows x 32 B ([C011] up to $1E): $C018-$C3D7; each 00:1720 call copies up to 18 rows (b stops at $12, 00:1763-1766) of the bank-$29 source to $C018+32[C010]. Maximum extent not derived ([C010] is data-dependent). Rows are streamed to $9800+ by 09:41FF/4234 with 05F8.

name: [6] quadrant composite pieces (top-right, etc.)
type: 8 tiles ($80 B) per tile row x 7 rows, row stride $100
notes: 06:5871 builds a 2x2 composite of 4 photos: [$D7F9] -> $C000, [$D7FB] -> $C080, [$D7FA] -> $C700, [$D7FC] -> $C780 (offsets passed in HL, 06:5877-5889), each piece = 7 tile rows x $80 B copied with call $0450 (stride $100, 06:58D3-58EC); then the album-layout upload 06:5895-58B3.

name: [4] icon tile buffer 2 (30 tiles)
notes: Second icon plane (inverted mask), uploaded to $8520 (bc=$01E0).

name: [5] 160x16-px band: curve plot / text line
type: 20 x 2 tiles (2 tile rows of 20 tiles x 16 B = $280 bytes; row 0 $C200-$C33F, row 1 $C340-$C47F)
notes: Cleared by 05:5FAE; ruler marks at $C210, $C250, $C291, $C2D0, $C310 (05:5FBC-5FD6, 16 bytes of $01 each, second tile row +$130); horizontal lines at $C220 (top, both planes, 05:5FFF) and $C36E/$C36F (bottom, one plane each, 05:600D); four curve drawers read the 32 bytes $D965-$D984 two per tile column (05:5ED2-5EFB, ld b,$10) and set pixel groups with masks $E0/$0E (05:601A/604D). Alternatively 05:60EE renders a 20-character line (source row at $C480) with the font tiles of bank $10 $7600 (call $1615, 16 bytes per glyph; top half at $C200+16i, bottom half +$140). The band is handed to 00:19EB (ld hl,$C200 ; ld a,1, 05:59EC-59F1), which stores HL in $DC21:$DC22 and A+1 in $DC3E (00:1A08-1A12); $0280 = exactly one Game Boy Printer data packet (00:1A48, 00:1A7B) -> I: this is a printer band.

name: [6]/[0A] effect region: tile (3,3)
notes: Entry of the block routine 06:76C0 (a=8) in the region-entry list 06:73EF-7477; the 0A twin (0A:5A19-5A1C) copies sensor-buffer data from SRAM $A430 to $C330. Block size/shape: ?.

name: [4] icon source graphics (blit source)
notes: Sprite graphics for the software blit 00:1EA4 (record bytes 2-4 = {$C0,$C3,$00} = source $C3C0, bank/WRAM 0) and for the icon builders.

name: [6]/[0A] effect region: row 4
notes: Entry 06:746F-7474 (a=$0A, jp $7480); 0A:5A0D-5A18 copies SRAM $A500 -> $C400, 10 tile rows (b=$0A, helper 0A:5100): tile rows 4-13.

name: [5] 20-tile text/notes source line
type: 20 tile codes: 9F x5, 4F, 9F x4, 4F, 9F x4, 4F, 9F x4 template, filled in place
notes: The 20-byte template at 05:5C7E is copied to $C480 (05:5C0C-5C19), then 4 groups of 5 bytes are filled from 4 values (ld hl,$D9BD ...): value 0 -> blank $8A; else 2 glyph bytes from the 12-entry table 05:5C92 (value-1 mod 12) and an octave digit tile quotient+$23 at $C481+5k..$C483+5k, and an attribute-like byte $F0|.. at $C484+5k (05:5C59-5C76). $C486 also receives a 1-3 digit decimal ([$D9D1], via 05:60BF, 05:5E55-5E5B). The line is then rendered into $C200 (05:5C78 -> 60EE). Note names (12 glyph pairs 09 9F, 09 20, 0A 9F, ... = A, A#, B, ...) and the [$D9BD]/[$D9CD] source are I.

name: [4] icon source mask (blit mask)
notes: Mask for the blit (record bytes 5-7 = {$A0,$C5,$00} = $C5A0) and source of buffer 2.

name: [0A] second write cursor (mirror)
notes: 0A:5577-55B9: copies 7 tile rows of the SRAM sensor buffer ($A800...) to $C700... (DE, forward) and writes every byte pair also through BC: BC starts at $C60E (last pixel row of tile 0 of tile row 6), goes backwards inside each tile (inc c ... dec c x3 = -2 per pair, 0A:558B-5597), forward tile by tile (add c,$20, 0A:55A6-55AA) and one tile row up per source row (dec b, 0A:55B5): the top half becomes the vertical mirror image of the bottom half (I). Which Trick uses it: ?.

name: [6]/[0A] photo tile row 7 (halves $C700/$C780)
notes: Entry points (HL = $C700 or $C780, a=7 tile rows) of the region routines 06:758F/7480; 0A:590C copies SRAM $A800 -> $C700 (7 rows), 0A:5A70 copies $A880 -> $C780. See the photo-image row.

name: [0] software sprite-to-BG blit: patch list
type: entries of 5 bytes: addr_lo, addr_hi, and_mask, or_byte0, or_byte1; list ended by a zero address word
notes: 00:1EA4 copies an 8-byte sprite record (width px, height px, source ptr/bank, mask ptr/bank) to $FFD5-$FFDC, then builds for every pixel row x tile column one entry: the VRAM address of the 2-byte pixel row (from the table 00:2170), an AND mask ($FFE7/$FFE6, from 00:1FA2/1FAA) and two OR bytes; 00:213D applies the list during HBlank (waits LY in $20-$87 and STAT mode 0, 00:2153-2161): [addr] = ([addr] & mask) | or0, [addr+1] = ([addr+1] & mask) | or1. Entry count = pixel rows x tile columns (records in bank 4 $56BF-$56F1 reach 40x48 px -> up to ~$5A0 bytes, I). Overlaps the photo buffer $C800-$CDFF, but the photo has already been uploaded to VRAM when bank 4 calls it.

name: [0] blit patch list: first entry AND mask
notes: Third byte of entry 0 (see $C800).

name: [0] blit patch list: first entry OR bytes (cleared)
notes: Fourth/fifth byte of entry 0, zeroed by 00:209C before ORing.

name: [6]/[0A] effect region: row 10
notes: Entry 06:745F-7464 (a=4, jp $7480); 0A:59F5-5A00 copies SRAM $AB00 -> $CA00, 4 tile rows (10-13).

name: [0A] second write cursor (mirror)
notes: Same pattern as $C60E in 0A:55BA-55FC: SRAM $A100... is copied to $C000... (7 tile rows, forward) and mirrored through BC from $CD0E upwards, so the bottom half becomes the vertical mirror of the top half (I).

name: Thumbnail (slot bytes E00-EFF)
type: 4x4 tiles x 16 B, 2bpp; valid area 32x28 px, 1-px frame
notes: Cleared (02:471D-4723, 02:47DE-47E4), built from the photo by 00:2583 (02:472C, 02:47ED; HL -> 3-byte record {$00,$C0,$00} at 02:47B3 = source $C000 in WRAM, bc=$CE00 destination) and framed by 00:296F (a=3 = both planes: top row, bottom line at pixel row 27, left/right columns). 00:2583 produces only 4 pixel rows for the last tile row (b=2 on the last pass, 00:25AA-25AF), so the bottom 4 pixel rows of tiles 12-15 are never generated (correction to README 3.3 "32x32 px": the image is 32x28). An album copy gets a badge stamped by 00:29F9 (ld d,$CE, six (offset,or,xor) triples at ROM $2A11). Uploaded to VRAM $9600 by 09:45B0-45E8: $CE00-$CEC7 (200 bytes) and the first 8 bytes of tiles 13-15 ($CED0/$CEE0/$CEF0) - exactly the generated area. The same page is re-used by bank 7 as a motion-path table (overlay row below).

name: [7] motion-path table (x,y pairs)
type: byte pairs: x at $CE00+2n, y at $CE01+2n, n = step
notes: 07:6557 decodes a delta-coded list (run lengths with bit 7 = repeat, running sum in A) into every second byte of $CE00 (ld [de],a ; inc de ; inc de, 07:6565-656B, 07:6573-6578), once for x then once for y (b=2, de +1 after the first pass, 07:657D-657F). 07:6387 (object index in E, 0..2) reads (x,y) for the current step (bc=$CE00, [$D83C+2e] = step, 07:63B2-641B) and 07:6424 reads $D502+e-indexed words from a second table. Number of steps per path: not derived (?); it overwrites the thumbnail page, so the bank-7 animation screens do not display a thumbnail. Which screens are these (mode $0E 07:4000 / $07?): ?.

name: Tag: owner copy F00-F11
notes: On a new shot 02:46F0 copies 18 bytes from the camera-owner buffer $DA49-$DA5A (02:4742-4747) into both tag copies (primary at $CF00, echo at $CF5C, loop 02:473C-4780, de=0 then $5C) and zeroes the next $43 bytes F12-F54 (02:474A-474C). For a received picture the same bytes arrive inside the link buffer (they are the original photographer's owner block) and are not rewritten by 02:462F.

name: Tag: reception counters F12-F14
notes: 02:462F (store a received picture): +1 on F12 if [$DA56] bit 0, on F13 if bit 1, on F14 always (cap $63, 00:4668-4684), once for each tag copy (de=0, then $5C). Zeroed by a new shot (02:474A). Only 02:462F increments them.

name: Tag: F15-F32 (comments + 3 zero bytes)
notes: Not accessed individually in proven code of this range; comments are written to SRAM directly (02:494B, per README). Zeroed by 02:46F0 (c=$43 from $CF12), carried unchanged through the link buffer.

name: Tag: copy flag F33
notes: Album Copy (02:45A1) sets [$CF33]=1 (02:45CA) and the echo [$CF8F] (02:45CD); the editor save-back 02:47C4 reads $CF33 and, if non-zero, re-stamps the thumbnail badge (02:47F8-4800, ld d,$CE / call $29F9).

name: Tag: photo checksum F34-F35
notes: Stored from $DA8F/$DA90 (computed by 02:4005 over the photo bytes at shot time, called from 02:46FA) into both tag copies; not refreshed by the editor (02:47C4 never touches it).

name: Tag: hotspot fields F36-F53
type: 5 flags, 5 X, 5 Y, 5 sound, 5 effect, 5 jump
notes: Zeroed in both copies when a received picture is stored (02:462F) and (as part of F12-F54) at a new shot. Hotspot editing writes SRAM directly, not this buffer.

name: Tag: Magic
notes: 5 bytes copied from ROM 02:4000; the 2 checksum bytes F5A-F5B are then computed over $5A bytes by 02:432F (bc=$005A, 02:46A7, 02:4774).

name: Tag echo F5C-FB7
notes: Second tag copy ($CF5C+x = $CF00+x + $5C). $CF8F = echo of F33. $CFB8 is the first byte not stored.

name: Beyond the slot image
notes: $CFB8-$CFFE is neither loaded (bc=$0FB8, 02:4CA8) nor stored (bc=$0FB8, 02:46CA); only cleared with the rest (07:43E9-43EF, 07:475D-4763, 06:5E5A-5E60: bc=$1000).

name: Link buffer: gender/blood byte of the sender
notes: Last byte of the $1000-byte exchange area. Written with the own [$DA56] before the exchange; read at 07:4A24 as a bit mask (bit 0 -> $DA9E, bit 1 -> $DA9F, BCD +1 capped at $99, 07:4A17-4A41: the camera-level counters 10C3/10C4). Because the exchange swaps the whole $1000-byte buffer in place, the value read after the exchange is the peer's byte (I: no instruction states that $CFFF travels, the loop bound is [$DC47] = $10 pages).

name: [7] collision mask 0 (silhouette of image A)
type: 56 bytes = 8 columns x 7 rows of 8x8-px cells; non-zero = cell contains pixels
notes: 00:1668 runs 00:16C4 three times (de=$D000, $D040, $D080; photo pointer via 05:7F69, c=2,0,1, 00:1672-169F): for each of 56 cells (b=$38) the 16 source bytes are ORed into one byte (00:16DC-16E8). 07:66E9-6735 checks eight moving objects ($D81F+c, $D827+c, c=7..0, 07:66EF-6738) against the cell $D000 + 64[$D866] + (y_cell8 + x_cell) (07:6705-672F, [$D866] selects mask 0/1/2 = x64); a non-zero cell calls 07:673B (hit counter $D865, state $D502). So the three masks are per-image hit maps of a bank-7 mini-game (I: which game).

name: [5] BG-row buffer (20 tiles)
notes: 05:51C9 copies 20 bytes from bank $27 $5AB0 (call $0450), then, depending on [$D8B4/$D8B5/$D8B6] and the per-channel arrays [$D945+..], [$D98A+..], [$D9B1+..] and the hardware sound registers [$FF26]/[$FF12], overlays 4-byte glyph groups from ROM 05:5274/5278/527C/5280/5284 at $D000, $D004, $D008, $D00C, $D010 (05:5267-5272), and uploads the 20 bytes to BG row $9EC0 (05:5258-5263). Looks like a per-channel activity strip of the sound/music screen (I).

name: [0] image-reducer result pair
notes: 00:289C combines two source bytes (each nibble mapped through the 16-entry table at ROM $36F0, 00:289E-28BF) into two result bytes $D000, $D001; the 2:1 reducers 00:2656, 00:2734, 00:27F4 read them back. Shared with the bank-5 and bank-7 uses below (never simultaneously).

name: [0] image-reducer accumulators
notes: 00:25B6-25D4: for each 4-source-byte group the pair at [hl] is zeroed (ld [hl+],a ; ld [hl],a) and then, four times (ld c,4), the high nibble of the value returned by 00:261B is added to the first byte and the low nibble to the second (00:25C4-25CE); 00:261B reads two source bytes at [DE] and returns tbl[x] + 2tbl[y] (tbl = 256-byte table at ROM $3700, ld h,$37 at 00:2622, 00:2628); inc hl moves to the next pair, 8 pairs in all = $D002-$D011. 00:2631 (HL=$D002, DE=$0080, then HL=$D004, DE=$0008) reads every other pair, adds d/e, thresholds (swap, srl, rl c/rl b) into two output bytes (BC), which 00:25E3-25F4 store in the destination tile. This explains all of $D002, $D004, $D006, $D008, $D00A, $D00C, $D00E, $D010 appearing as constants.

name: [7] collision mask 1
notes: Second mask ([$D866] = 1).

name: [7] collision mask 2
notes: Third mask ([$D866] = 2).

name: Print-animation packet buffer
type: VRAM packet: H L ctl + 16 data bytes + 00
notes: $D200=$8F, $D201=$E0 (VRAM $8FE0), $D202=$10 (ctl: 16 plain bytes), $D203-$D212 = 16 tile bytes copied (call $0450, 08:4ECF) from bank $21 $7BB0 + 16[$D500], $D213=0 terminator; then bc=$D200 / a=0 / call $0A8A queues it and [$D500] is incremented modulo 5 (08:4EEC-4EF5). It updates one tile ($8FE0) with a 5-frame animation. Only bank 8 builds packets in proven code.

name: VRAM write queue (ring buffer)
type: 64 entries x 4 bytes FF, ptr_lo, ptr_hi, bank; page $D3
notes: Write index $D520, read index $D521 (byte offsets inside page $D3, only L is incremented so they wrap at 256; zeroed at boot 00:01B6-01B9). Enqueue 00:0A8A: A=bank, BC=packet pointer -> [l]=$FF, [l+1]=C, [l+2]=B, [l+3]=A, [l+4]=0, index += 4 (the trailing 0 is the end marker and is overwritten by the next entry). Dequeue loops while the flag byte at the read index is non-zero, switches ROM bank to the entry bank and runs 00:0AE7 on the packet: records H L ctl data... (VRAM address, control, data), the list ends when the next H is 0; ctl bit 7 = column mode (address step $20), bit 6 = repeat one data byte, low 6 bits = count. When the LCD is off the queue is flushed at once (00:0AA6-0AB2). Only bank 8 enqueues in proven code (08:4EE9, 08:5290).

name: OAM shadow buffer
notes: Source of the VBlank OAM DMA (page $D4, 00:03F0). 00:0895 fills all 160 bytes with $F0 (Y=240, off-screen) and zeroes the cursor $FF9A. Adders append at $D400 + [$FF9A] (ldh a,[$FF9A] / ld l,a / ld h,$D4) and write the cursor back (00:24E4-24E5, 00:2576-2577, 04:5316-5317); 00:08A4 re-fills from the cursor to $D49F with $F0 (guard cp $A0) and zeroes the cursor. Adders (00:2464, 247D, 2496, 24AF, 250A): A = template number (x2 = index), table of word pointers at bank 2 $6E4B / bank 2 $5272 / bank 1 $5D47 / bank 1 $4000; a template is a list of 4-byte records (Y+C, X+B, tile, attr) ended by a first byte $80; 250A adds a byte read from the stack frame (ld hl,sp+$07, 00:256B) to each tile number. 04:5307-5336 builds 16 sprites directly: Y = [$DADC+i]+8, X = [$DACC+i], tile = $70+i, attr 0. The adders have no bounds check (only 00:08A4 tests $A0).

name: (after the OAM shadow) free
notes: No proven access; the DMA reads only $D400-$D49F. A sprite list longer than 40 entries would spill into it unchecked (never DMA'd).

name: Stack (top of WRAM)
notes: No absolute access in the table. Run-time depth cannot be bounded statically (nested far calls push return address + bank, 00:08C1; VBlank pushes 4 registers 00:02A3-02A6 plus the handler call chain). The next object below is outside this region ($DD.. is described in wram_dc00).

name: Initial SP value (top of stack)
notes: Only used as the immediate of ld sp,$DFFF; the byte itself is never addressed or pushed to (first push writes $DFFE,$DFFD); not cleared by the cold-boot clear (bc=$1FFF), cleared by the soft-reset clear (bc=$2000).
